title: Police Posed as a Busboy to Get a Killer's Pizza Crust

narration: A pizza crust helped catch the Gilgo Beach killer.
But it wasn't the first time.
shots.visual_description: gr15 pizzeria (warm grade); gr15_neighbour_a: sit -> present -> hands_together; gr15_neighbour_b: stand -> arms_crossed (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: callout 'A PIZZA CRUST', label 'GILGO BEACH · 2023', label 'THIRTEEN YEARS EARLIER...'.

sources.claim_text: Gilgo Beach (Case File 07): prosecutors' July 2023 filing said DNA from a pizza crust Rex Heuermann discarded in Manhattan in January 2023 linked him to evidence in the case (a mitochondrial DNA link); he was arrested in July 2023 and pleaded guilty in April 2026. 'Helped catch' refers to that role in building the case.

About 13 years before Gilgo (2010 vs 2023), in July 2010, Los Angeles detectives used DNA from pizza and tableware Lonnie Franklin Jr. left at a restaurant to confirm him as the 'Grim Sleeper' suspect.

narration: In 1985, a killer began murdering women in South Los Angeles.
shots.visual_description: gr15 south la (night grade); detective: stand -> stand_tense -> arms_crossed (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'SOUTH LOS ANGELES · 1985'.

sources.claim_text: Franklin was convicted of murdering nine women and a 15-year-old girl in South Los Angeles between 1985 and 2007 (first conviction count: August 1985). He was not identified until 2010, about 25 years after the first of those killings. Summary only; no detail used.

narration: He then seemed to stop for about thirteen years.
A newspaper dubbed him the Grim Sleeper.
shots.visual_description: task force (cold grade); analyst: sit_type -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit; detective: stand -> arms_crossed -> bowed -> read_newspaper -> realise; keyed camera moves, handheld; overlays: svg, funfact 'LA Weekly coined 'Grim Sleeper' / in 2008, for an apparent gap / in the killings: 1988 to 2002.'.

overlays.text: LA Weekly coined 'Grim Sleeper' / in 2008, for an apparent gap / in the killings: 1988 to 2002.

sources.claim_text: FUN FACT: the nickname 'Grim Sleeper' was coined by LA Weekly (reporter Christine Pelisek and her editor) in 2008, because of an apparent gap in the killings between 1988 and 2002 (reported as 13 or 14 years); the LAPD later adopted it. Police later said they did not believe there had really been a break, so the narration says he 'seemed to stop'.

narration: Most of his victims were young Black women.
A community group spent decades demanding justice.
shots.visual_description: courthouse night (night grade); gr15_neighbour_a: stand -> hands_together -> point_up -> stand (walks); gr15_neighbour_b: read -> present -> arms_crossed (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'SOUTH LA · 1985-2007', card 'A COMMUNITY GROUP, FROM THE 1980s: / BLACK COALITION FIGHTING / BACK SERIAL MURDERS / PRESSING FOR ANSWERS'.

overlays.text: A COMMUNITY GROUP, FROM THE 1980s: / BLACK COALITION FIGHTING / BACK SERIAL MURDERS / PRESSING FOR ANSWERS

sources.claim_text: Most of the victims were Black women, many in their twenties and thirties (the youngest was 15), in South Los Angeles.

The Black Coalition Fighting Back Serial Murders, founded in the mid-1980s by Margaret Prescod and others, pressed the LAPD and the city for answers and kept campaigning for justice for the victims; after the 2016 verdict Prescod said the group had been fighting for justice since 1985.

narration: Police had the killer's DNA, but no name.
shots.visual_description: gr15 dna lab (cold grade); gr15_criminalist: examine -> present -> stand_tense; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'CRIME-SCENE DNA'.

sources.claim_text: Investigators had crime-scene DNA from the killer, but it did not identically match anyone in California's offender DNA database; a first familial search for the case (2008) found no relative either.

narration: In 2010, California searched its DNA database for his relatives.
It flagged a close relative: his son.
shots.visual_description: office day (cold grade); analyst: sit_type -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit; gr15_detective: stand -> read -> stand_tense (walks); camera push/pull; overlays: label 'CALIFORNIA · APRIL 2010', card 'THE STATE SEARCH FLAGGED / A CLOSE RELATIVE: HIS SON / Not named here, and not a suspect.'.

overlays.text: THE STATE SEARCH FLAGGED / A CLOSE RELATIVE: HIS SON / Not named here, and not a suspect.

sources.claim_text: A second familial DNA search of California's offender database, begun on 28 April 2010, found a partial match indicating a close male relative of the killer: Franklin's son. (Why the son's profile was on file is not narrated; he is not named or shown and is not suggested to have done anything wrong.)

narration: The son's father: Lonnie David Franklin Junior.
shots.visual_description: gr15 south la (warm grade); gr15_franklin (silhouette): stand -> stand -> hands_together -> stand (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: card 'THE SON'S FATHER: / LONNIE DAVID / FRANKLIN JR. / 57 · SOUTH LOS ANGELES'.

sources.claim_text: The son's father was Lonnie David Franklin Jr., then 57, who lived in South Los Angeles (West 81st Street).

narration: Detectives needed his own DNA.
They followed him to a pizza restaurant in Buena Park.
shots.visual_description: gr15 pizzeria (warm grade); gr15_franklin (silhouette): sit -> hands_together -> sit; gr15_detective: stand -> stand_tense -> sit -> sit_read (walks); keyed camera moves, handheld; overlays: label 'LAPD · JULY 2010', label 'BUENA PARK · 5 JULY 2010'.
shots.reconstruction_tag: ILLUSTRATION · NOT A LIKENESS · GENERIC RESTAURANT

sources.claim_text: On 5 July 2010, LAPD detectives followed Franklin to a birthday party at a pizza restaurant in Buena Park, California.

narration: Inside, one detective posed as a busboy.
He cleared Franklin's plates, and kept the pizza crust.
shots.visual_description: gr15 pizzeria (warm grade); gr15_franklin (silhouette): sit -> hands_together; gr15_busboy: stand -> present -> determined (walks); keyed camera moves, handheld; overlays: label 'UNDERCOVER, AS A BUSBOY', card 'WHAT HE COLLECTED, AS REPORTED: / NAPKINS · A GLASS · A FORK / AND THE PIZZA CRUST', callout 'THE CRUST'.

overlays.text: WHAT HE COLLECTED, AS REPORTED: / NAPKINS · A GLASS · A FORK / AND THE PIZZA CRUST

shots.reconstruction_tag: ILLUSTRATION · NOT A LIKENESS · GENERIC RESTAURANT

sources.claim_text: An undercover LAPD detective, in a restaurant uniform, posed as a busboy (some reports: a waiter or employee) and collected items Franklin used: napkins, a glass, a fork or silverware, and a partially eaten slice of pizza / leftover pizza crust. A judge later ruled the DNA was lawfully obtained.

narration: The DNA matched the crime scenes.
shots.visual_description: gr15 dna lab (cold grade); gr15_criminalist: examine -> stand -> realise -> point; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'THE LAB · JULY 2010', stamp 'MATCH'.

sources.claim_text: DNA from the items collected at the restaurant matched DNA evidence from the crime scenes.

narration: Two days later, police arrested him outside his home.
shots.visual_description: gr15 south la (cold grade); gr15_franklin (silhouette): stand -> stand_tense -> hands_behind (walks); gr15_detective: stand -> present (walks); agent_a: stand -> stand_tense (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label '7 JULY 2010 · SOUTH LA'.
shots.reconstruction_tag: ILLUSTRATION · NOT A LIKENESS · GENERIC HOUSE

sources.claim_text: Franklin was arrested on 7 July 2010 (two days after the party) in front of his home on West 81st Street in South Los Angeles.

narration: Officials called it California's first familial DNA arrest.
shots.visual_description: press room (cold grade); agent_a: arms_crossed -> stand; official: hands_together -> present -> point_up -> hands_together; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'LOS ANGELES · JULY 2010', funfact 'Officials said it was the first arrest / from California's familial / DNA search program.'.

overlays.text: Officials said it was the first arrest / from California's familial / DNA search program.

sources.claim_text: FUN FACT: officials described it as the first arrest produced by California's familial DNA search program (the Attorney General's office said the program had led to its first arrest; District Attorney Steve Cooley called it the first successful use of a familial search in California). Attributed to officials on screen.

narration: In 2016, a jury convicted him of ten murders.
Sentenced to death, he died in prison in 2020.
shots.visual_description: courtroom (cold grade); judge (silhouette): sit -> gavel -> sit -> sit_read; examiner (silhouette): sit -> sit_read; gr15_franklin (silhouette): sit -> stand -> hands_together -> bowed; camera push/pull; overlays: card '5 MAY 2016 · JURY VERDICT / GUILTY OF 10 MURDERS / AUG 2016: SENTENCED TO DEATH / DIED IN PRISON · MARCH 2020'.

overlays.text: 5 MAY 2016 · JURY VERDICT / GUILTY OF 10 MURDERS / AUG 2016: SENTENCED TO DEATH / DIED IN PRISON · MARCH 2020

sources.claim_text: On 5 May 2016 a Los Angeles jury convicted Franklin of 10 counts of first-degree murder (nine women and a 15-year-old girl) and one count of attempted murder.
The jury recommended death in June 2016; on 10 August 2016 Judge Kathleen Kennedy sentenced him to death.
Franklin died on 28 March 2020 at San Quentin State Prison, where he was on death row, aged 67; officials reported no signs of trauma.

narration: Nine women and a fifteen-year-old girl.
Some families waited decades.
shots.visual_description: gr15 south la (dawn grade); camera push/pull; overlays: svg.

sources.claim_text: The ten people he was convicted of murdering: Debra Jackson, Henrietta Wright, Barbara Ware, Bernita Sparks, Mary Lowe, Lachrica Jefferson, Alicia Alexander, Princess Berthomieux (15), Valerie McCorvey and Janecia Peters.
Some families waited decades: the earliest killings in the conviction date from 1985, the verdict came in 2016, and in 2016 families were still described as awaiting closure.

narration: Twenty-five years without a name. A pizza crust helped end it.
Next: a water bottle and the Boston Strangler.

An undercover LAPD detective, in a restaurant uniform, posed as a busboy (some reports: a waiter or employee) and collected items Franklin used: napkins, a glass, a fork or silverware, and a partially eaten slice of pizza / leftover pizza crust. A judge later ruled the DNA was lawfully obtained.

Next-case tease: in July 2013, almost 50 years after Mary Sullivan's 1964 killing, Boston investigators used DNA from a water bottle discarded by a nephew of Albert DeSalvo (the confessed Boston Strangler) to link the DeSalvo family to the crime-scene evidence; after his remains were exhumed, officials announced a DNA match to Sullivan's case only.
